problem: resolve_project_dir() does not prefer the exact encode_project() match, even though its docstring says it does. The exact dir starts with count 0, the loop then visits it again with its real count, and any sibling with the same loose key and more entries replaces it. Ties go to whichever dir os.listdir returns first.
failure: The exact dir '-Users-me-Dev-my-app' has 3 sessions and an unrelated sibling '-Users-me-Dev-myapp' has 40 entries. scope=current then returns myapp's transcripts even though the exact dir exists, and the report shows the wrong project's skills and corrections with no warning.
fix: Return the exact dir right away when os.path.isdir(exact) is true, and use the fuzzy search only as a fallback.

problem: _loose_key() removes every character outside [a-z0-9], including path separators and all non-ASCII. Different project paths can therefore get the same key, and the busiest one is scanned and labeled as the cwd project.
failure: '/Users/me/dev/my-app', '/Users/me/dev/myapp' and '/Users/me/dev/my/app' all get the same key. So do '/Users/me/문서' and '/Users/me/사진' (both become 'usersme'). Combined with the max-count rule, an unrelated project's transcripts are scanned in their place.
fix: Normalize only case and the '_'/'-' difference (for example, lower-case and map '_' to '-'). Keep separators and non-ASCII characters distinct.

problem: Only one matching dir is returned. In the case named in the commit message, where one repo's sessions are split across sibling dirs with different encodings, the sessions in the other dir are still silently ignored.
failure: A repo has 30 sessions under 'C--Dev-workspace-knue-patis' and 12 under 'c--dev-workspace_knue-patis'. Only the 30 are scanned, and the corrections, frictions and skill usage from the other 12 are dropped.
fix: Return every matching dir and scan each one in current and named scope.

problem: The root cause is that encode_project() does not match Claude Code's real encoding, which turns every non-alphanumeric character into '-', including '_', spaces and non-ASCII. The PR adds a lossy fuzzy fallback instead of fixing the encoder.
failure: For a path containing '_' or a space ('/x/my_repo', '/x/My Repo'), the exact candidate never exists, so every lookup goes through the fuzzy path where names can collide.
fix: Change encode_project to re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9]', '-', path) so the exact match works.

problem: The drift fix covers only current and --project scope. 'all' scope still lists each sibling dir with a different encoding as a separate project.
failure: One repo stored under two encodings shows up as two projects in 'all' scope. SKILL.md Step 4 then treats a pattern from that one repo as cross-project and recommends a global plugin asset for it.
fix: Group dirs by normalized key in 'all' scope so siblings are merged into one project.

problem: The 'most session files' tiebreak counts every directory entry (memory/, per-session UUID subdirs, tool-result dirs) instead of *.jsonl session files, as the docstring says it should.
failure: A sibling with 5 .jsonl files plus memory/ and 20 subagent subdirs (26 entries) beats a dir with 15 .jsonl files and few subdirs, so the dir with fewer sessions is chosen.
fix: Count glob('*.jsonl') to match how scan_dir counts sessions.

problem: The new os.listdir(proj_root) call in current and named scope has no error handling. The old exact-path lookup never listed proj_root, so this is a new way for the script to fail.
failure: If proj_root exists but cannot be read (permissions, or a broken CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR mount), PermissionError reaches main's catch-all and the script prints 'scan failed' and exits 1. Before this change it reported 'NO TRANSCRIPT DATA' and exited 0.
fix: Wrap os.listdir(proj_root) in try/except OSError and return exact on failure.

problem: The sibling reference that documents how the scanner finds the project dir was not updated for the new fuzzy fallback.
failure: A delegated subagent that follows transcript-format.md builds the exact encoded path and misses the sibling dirs the scanner now finds, so its ad-hoc greps disagree with the scanner's output.
fix: Update transcript-format.md to describe the fallback lookup rule the scanner now uses.

problem: This [FIX] commit has no regression test or reproduction step. That goes against docs/conventions.md ('[FIX] | Bug fix — requires reproduction step before fix') and the global rule 'Prefer regression tests for reproducible bugs'.
failure: No tmpdir fixture with sibling dirs that differ in encoding or collide exercises resolve_project_dir(), which is how the exact-match and collision bugs above went unnoticed.
fix: Add a --test fixture covering: exact dir exists alongside a larger sibling, a sibling that differs only in encoding, and a colliding unrelated project.
